title: Cities that refuse to swelter
text: Cities can run several degrees hotter {{1}} the countryside around them, {{2}} a result of dark roofs, bare asphalt and engines idling in the sun. The problem {{3}} worsened as summers lengthen, and it is the youngest and oldest residents {{4}} suffer most. Cities {{5}} fighting back with shade, water and pale surfaces: Paris is mapping its coolest walking routes, and Medellín planted {{6}} famous green corridors and watched peak temperatures fall by two degrees along them. {{7}} is usually the poorest districts, {{8}} have the fewest trees, that swelter worst — which is why urban heat is increasingly treated as a question of fairness rather than merely of comfort.

gaps.hint: preposition: ___ a result of dark roofs
gaps.explanation: 'As a result of' is the fixed phrase.
Present perfect with a singular subject: has worsened.
Cleft-supporting relative about people: residents who suffer.
Present continuous with a plural subject: are fighting.
The corridors belong to Medellín: its corridors.

gaps.hint: cleft pronoun: ___ is usually the poorest districts
gaps.explanation: The cleft structure emphasises the districts.

gaps.hint: relative: districts, ___ have the fewest trees
gaps.explanation: Non-defining relative after the pair of commas.
